title: "Agent-Level Correlation Analysis"
format: html
---

## What This Code Does

This demo runs a full simulation (30 agents, 100 days) and extracts agent-level data from the final epoch. It computes a Pearson correlation matrix across key agent variables: PSS-10, resilience, affect, resources, current stress, stress controllability, and stress overload.

The goal is to reveal how these variables co-vary at the individual agent level after the simulation has stabilised.

## Setup

```{python}
#| label: setup
import os
import sys
import pathlib
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

demos_dir = pathlib.Path(os.getcwd())
project_root = demos_dir.parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(project_root))

from src.python.model import StressModel
```

## Simulation

```{python}
#| label: simulate
days, agents, seed = 100, 30, 42
print(f"Running simulation with {agents} agents for {days} days (seed={seed})...")
model = StressModel(N=agents, max_days=days, seed=seed)
while model.running:
    model.step()

agent_data = model.get_agent_time_series_data()
final_step = agent_data["Step"].max()
final_epoch = agent_data[agent_data["Step"] == final_step].copy()
print(f"Simulation done. Final epoch data: {final_epoch.shape}")
```

## Correlation Matrix

```{python}
#| label: corr
vars_of_interest = ["pss10", "resilience", "affect", "resources", "current_stress", "stress_controllability", "stress_overload"]
available = [v for v in vars_of_interest if v in final_epoch.columns]
print(f"Analyzing: {available}")

corr = final_epoch[available].corr(method="pearson")
print(corr.to_string(float_format="%.4f"))
```

## Interpretation

```{python}
#| label: interpret
for i, v1 in enumerate(available):
    for j, v2 in enumerate(available):
        if i < j:
            r = corr.loc[v1, v2]
            strength = "Strong" if abs(r) > 0.7 else "Moderate" if abs(r) > 0.3 else "Weak"
            direction = "positive" if r > 0 else "negative"
            print(f"{v1} ↔ {v2}: {strength} {direction} (r={r:.4f})")
```

## Why This Matters for the Simulation

Agent-level correlations reveal the internal consistency of the model. For instance, if resilience and PSS-10 show a strong negative correlation, the model correctly captures the protective role of resilience against perceived stress. These diagnostics validate that agent-level mechanisms produce theoretically expected covariance patterns.
